page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs using the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processor, operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 7 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, falls within the middle 50% tier. While cached small-block memory read bandwidth is average at 1216.0 GB/sec, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 37.89 GB/sec. Conversely, large-block memory write speeds and database operations remain in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r8a.4xlarge offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without the premium of high-tier compute or GPU accelerators. The absence of local storage means storage costs are externalized to network volumes. This instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as database operations, caching layers like Redis, text processing, and general-purpose enterprise applications that do not require high-throughput sequential memory reads.
